result.title: Learning to Refer: Inference-Time Collaboration in Decentralized Federated Learning
result.summary: In decentralized federated learning, heterogeneous clients may develop complementary expertise, yet each query is typically evaluated only by the client where it arrives. To exploit this distributed expertise without global coordination, we formulate inference-time collaboration as budgeted local expert referral, a graph-constrained routing process in which a query can move only between neighboring clients and only visited clients contribute to its final prediction. EdgeDRM implements this framework by learning a density-based routing potential for each client: differences between neighboring potentials provide the comparisons used to select successive referrals, while local task models generate predictions that are aggregated along the resulting route. Both training and inference are decentralized, using only neighbor-local information without a central router or graph-wide client scoring. We establish estimation guarantees for the learned comparisons and characterize how local improvement and graph structure govern prior-weighted density gains from referral. Experiments on benchmark and real-world medical data show that EdgeDRM outperforms graph-matched decentralized baselines in most settings, with the clearest benefits under sparse connectivity.

AI.brief_summary: 提出「预算化本地专家转介」框架，把去中心化联邦学习的推理期协作建模为图约束路由过程：每个客户端学习基于密度的路由势，据此在邻居间逐跳转介查询，并沿路径聚合本地模型预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「逐跳转介＋预算限制＋沿路径聚合」的线索可供核查，或可类比 LVR 中动态计算分配、证据逐步获取与停止决策的状态更新设计；但原文不涉及视觉或多模态 latent 状态，迁移属推测。
